meta.title: The mental trick a Roman emperor used to shrink his problems

beats.text: When a worry grows too large, Marcus Aurelius did something strange. He flew.
In his mind he rose above the city, until streets became lines and crowds became dust.
Higher still — above the empire, above the sea, until the whole earth was a single point.
He pictured the vastness of time, too: the billions who lived before, the billions still to come.
From up there, the insult, the deadline, the quarrel — all of it shrinks to its true size.
He called it looking at human things from above. It is not escape. It is scale.
Next time your mind catastrophises, rise above it — and watch the problem grow small.
